raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Summary

- Fix `RuntimeError: get_heuristic_kernel_mla: cannot get heuristic kernel! gqa:8` when running sparse MLA models (e.g. GLM-5) with AITER enabled on ROCm at TP sizes that yield `num_heads < 16` per GPU
- Add head repeat padding logic to `ROCMAiterMLASparseImpl` (matching the existing workaround in `AiterMLAImpl`)
- Add validation in sparse backend selection so `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MLA=0` gives a clear error instead of silently failing
- Fix `ZeroDivisionError` in FP8 paged MQA logits indexer for small head counts (`heads < 64`)

## Root Cause

### Issue 1: MLA decode kernel crash (gqa=8)

The AITER MLA decode kernel (`mla_decode_stage1_asm_fwd`) only supports `num_heads >= 16`. GLM-5 has 64 attention heads; with TP=8, each GPU gets 8 heads, triggering the unsupported `gqa=8` code path.

The non-sparse `AiterMLAImpl` already handles this by repeating query heads from 8 to 16 before the kernel call and slicing every other head from the output. The sparse `ROCMAiterMLASparseImpl` was missing this logic.

Additionally, the sparse backend selection path (`_get_backend_priorities` in `rocm.py`) was hardcoded to `ROCM_AITER_MLA_SPARSE` without checking `is_mla_enabled()`, so `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MLA=0` had no effect for sparse models.

### Issue 2: FP8 indexer ZeroDivisionError

The sparse attention indexer calls `deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits_stage1` with default `ChunkQ=64`. When `heads < 64` (e.g. 8 with GLM-5 TP=8), the computation `heads // ChunkQ = 0` leads to `TileQCount = 0` and a `ZeroDivisionError`. Fixed by passing `ChunkQ=heads` explicitly, matching how the main `deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits` function handles it.

Related: https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/issues/726 (upstream feature request for native nhead=8 support)

## Test plan
- [x] Run GLM-5 FP8 with AITER enabled on ROCm TP=8 — verify no `gqa:8` crash and no ZeroDivisionError
- [x] Run DeepSeek-V3.2 (sparse MLA) at TP sizes yielding num_heads=8 — verify correctness
- [x] Verify existing sparse MLA tests still pass (num_heads >= 16 path unchanged)
- [ ] Verify `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MLA=0` now raises a clear ValueError for sparse models

### What changed

The previous version of this PR carried an inline head-repeat workaround in `ROCMAiterMLASparseImpl._forward_mla`. Since then, `AiterMLAHelper` (from `vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/rocm_aiter_mla.py`) was merged and is already wired into the sparse impl on main — it now does the `>= 16` head padding via `get_mla_padded_q` / `get_mla_unpadded_o`. So the MLA decode side of this PR is no longer needed and has been dropped.

What remains is a focused two-file delta (+35/-2):

1. **`vllm/v1/attention/ops/rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py`** — gate the AITER MQA logits kernels (`rocm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits` and `rocm_fp8_mqa_logits`) on `heads >= 16` and fall back to the existing PyTorch reference path otherwise. AITER `deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits[_stage1]` / `fp8_mqa_logits` still require `heads >= 16` (https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/issues/2563), which crashes the indexer for models like GLM-5 with TP=8 (8 heads/GPU). The previous module-level `_AITER_MQA_SMALL_HEADS_WARNED` global is gone — replaced with `logger.warning_once(..., scope="local")` as requested.

2. **`vllm/platforms/rocm.py`** — `_get_backend_priorities` now raises `ValueError` when sparse MLA is requested but AITER MLA is disabled (instead of returning `[]`, which only surfaces as a confusing downstream error in `v1/attention/selector.py`). This also addresses @AndreasKaratzas's and @Rohan138's earlier comments.

### Verification

- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check`: clean.
- Functional test still applicable: GLM-5 with `tensor_parallel_size=8` (8 heads/GPU) on MI355X no longer crashes in the indexer when AITER is enabled with FP8 KV cache; falls back to the PyTorch reference and warns once per process.

The MLA-decode head-repeat workaround was dropped entirely since `AiterMLAHelper.get_mla_padded_q`/`get_mla_unpadded_o` on `main` already handle the `>= 16` padding.
- **@AndreasKaratzas** — `_get_backend_priorities` now raises a `ValueError` with an actionable message when sparse MLA is requested without AITER MLA enabled, instead of returning `[]` and surfacing a confusing downstream error in the selector.

What remains is purely the indexer fix: gate AITER's `deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits` / `fp8_mqa_logits` on `heads >= 16` and fall back to the PyTorch reference otherwise. issue_comments.body: cc @zejun-chen @wuhuikx @gbyu-amd @tjtanaa - Could you please review this PR? It fixes the AITER sparse MLA crash for models with num_heads < 16 (e.g., GLM-5 with TP=8). The fix adds head repeat/unrepeat logic mirroring the non-sparse AiterMLAImpl, plus a guard in the backend selector when AITER MLA is disabled. Thanks!

Hi team — friendly ping on this PR. It fixes two blocking issues for running sparse MLA models (e.g., GLM-5) with AITER on ROCm when num_heads < 16:

1. **`RuntimeError: get_heuristic_kernel_mla: cannot get heuristic kernel! gqa:8`** — adds head-repeat padding to `ROCMAiterMLASparseImpl`, matching the existing workaround in `AiterMLAImpl` (merged in #35850)
2. **`ZeroDivisionError` in FP8 paged MQA logits** — passes `ChunkQ=heads` explicitly for small head counts

All NVIDIA CI checks pass. The AMD CI run was canceled (not failed) and needs to be retriggered.

@tjtanaa @gshtras @AndreasKaratzas — could you help review/approve when you get a chance? This unblocks GLM-5 MXFP4 benchmarking work on MI355. Thanks!

cc @gshtras @tjtanaa @BowenBao @wufann — Requesting expedited review. This PR fixes **AITER sparse MLA crash for num_heads < 16** (GLM-5 with TP=8 gives 8 heads/GPU), which is a blocker for GLM-5 inference on MI355X. Part of a customer-facing series — see also #38665 and #38947.

@robertgshaw2-redhat — addressed your global-variable comment and rebased on latest `main`. Re-pinging for review/merge.

### What changed

The previous version of this PR carried an inline head-repeat workaround in `ROCMAiterMLASparseImpl._forward_mla`. Since then, `AiterMLAHelper` (from `vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/rocm_aiter_mla.py`) was merged and is already wired into the sparse impl on main — it now does the `>= 16` head padding via `get_mla_padded_q` / `get_mla_unpadded_o`. So the MLA decode side of this PR is no longer needed and has been dropped.

What remains is a focused two-file delta (+35/-2):

1. **`vllm/v1/attention/ops/rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py`** — gate the AITER MQA logits kernels (`rocm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits` and `rocm_fp8_mqa_logits`) on `heads >= 16` and fall back to the existing PyTorch reference path otherwise. AITER `deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits[_stage1]` / `fp8_mqa_logits` still require `heads >= 16` (https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/issues/2563), which crashes the indexer for models like GLM-5 with TP=8 (8 heads/GPU). The previous module-level `_AITER_MQA_SMALL_HEADS_WARNED` global is gone — replaced with `logger.warning_once(..., scope="local")` as requested.

2. **`vllm/platforms/rocm.py`** — `_get_backend_priorities` now raises `ValueError` when sparse MLA is requested but AITER MLA is disabled (instead of returning `[]`, which only surfaces as a confusing downstream error in `v1/attention/selector.py`). This also addresses @AndreasKaratzas's and @Rohan138's earlier comments.

### Verification

- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check`: clean.
- Functional test still applicable: GLM-5 with `tensor_parallel_size=8` (8 heads/GPU) on MI355X no longer crashes in the indexer when AITER is enabled with FP8 KV cache; falls back to the PyTorch reference and warns once per process.

AI assistance was used to scope down the rebase against `AiterMLAHelper`. I've reviewed each line.

cc @tjtanaa — rebased and addressed Robert's review (replaced the global with logger.warning_once). The PR now slims to a +35/-2 two-file delta since AiterMLAHelper on main supersedes the original inline head-repeat workaround. Could you take another quick look when you have a minute? Thanks.

@dllehr-amd @AndreasKaratzas @robertgshaw2-redhat — rebased onto latest `main` and this is now `MERGEABLE` (no conflicts). Slimmed to a focused +36/-5 two-file delta.

Review items addressed:

- **@robertgshaw2-redhat** — the module-level `_AITER_MQA_SMALL_HEADS_WARNED` global is gone; both fallbacks now use `logger.warning_once(..., scope="local")` as requested. The MLA-decode head-repeat workaround was dropped entirely since `AiterMLAHelper.get_mla_padded_q`/`get_mla_unpadded_o` on `main` already handle the `>= 16` padding.
- **@AndreasKaratzas** — `_get_backend_priorities` now raises a `ValueError` with an actionable message when sparse MLA is requested without AITER MLA enabled, instead of returning `[]` and surfacing a confusing downstream error in the selector.

What remains is purely the indexer fix: gate AITER's `deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits` / `fp8_mqa_logits` on `heads >= 16` and fall back to the PyTorch reference otherwise. AITER's kernels require `heads >= 16` (upstream tracked in https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/issues/2563), which is what crashes the indexer for GLM-5 with TP=8 (8 heads/GPU).

Could you take another look / approve for merge? This unblocks GLM-5 sparse-MLA inference on MI355X. Thanks!

## Code Review

This pull request addresses a crash in sparse MLA on ROCm when the number of attention heads per GPU is less than 16. The fix introduces head-repetition padding in `ROCMAiterMLASparseImpl`, mirroring an existing workaround, to ensure compatibility with the AITER MLA decode kernel. Additionally, it adds validation to provide a clear error message if sparse MLA is used without AITER MLA being enabled, improving the user experience. The changes are well-implemented and effectively resolve the reported issue.
LGTM, some minor suggestions and questions.
